1002	## `pre_actions` versus `tools`
1003	
1004	The placement decides who fires the call.
1005	
1006	| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
1007	|---|---|---|---|
1008	| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
1009	| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
1010	| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |
1011	
1012	The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.
1013	
1014	**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.
1015	
1016	**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.
1017	
1018	Differences in behaviour:
1019	
1020	| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
1021	|---|---|---|
1022	| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
1023	| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
1024	| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
1025	| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
1026	| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |
1027	
1028	To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.
1029	
1030	### A `pre_actions` node
1031	
1032	```json
1033	{
1034	  "name": "fetch_order",
1035	  "node_type": "api_request",
1036	  "passthrough": true,
1037	  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
1038	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
1039	  "pre_actions": [
1040	    {
1041	      "type": "function",
1042	      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
1043	      "function": {
1044	        "name": "get_order",
1045	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
1046	        "description": "Get the order.",
1047	        "parameters": {
1048	          "type": "object",
1049	          "properties": {
1050	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
1051	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
1052	            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
1053	            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
1054	          }
1055	        }
1056	      }
1057	    }
1058	  ],
1059	  "response_mapping": [
1060	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
1061	  ],
1062	  "transitions": [
1063	    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
1064	  ]
1065	}
1066	```
1067	
1068	The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.
1069	
1070	### Tool descriptions
1071	
1072	In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.
1073	
1074	- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
1075	- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
1076	- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
1077	- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
1078	- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".
1079	
1080	A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."
1081	
1082	## `response_mapping`
1083	
1084	`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.
1085	
1086	```json
1087	{
1088	  "response_mapping": [
1089	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
1090	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
1091	  ]
1092	}
1093	```
1094	
1095	| Field | Meaning |
1096	|---|---|
1097	| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
1098	| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |
1099	
1100	### Placement
1101	
1102	- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
1103	- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.
1104	
1105	`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.
1106	
1107	### Where a result lands (trial findings)
1108	
1109	Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.
1110	
1111	```json
1112	{
1113	  "status": "success",
1114	  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
1115	  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
1116	  "status_code": 200,
1117	  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
1118	}
1119	```
1120	
1121	`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.
1122	
1123	The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:
1124	
1125	| Variable | Value |
1126	|---|---|
1127	| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
1128	| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
1129	| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
1130	| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
1131	| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
1132	| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
1133	| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
1134	| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
1135	| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
1136	| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |
1137	
1138	Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.
1139	
1140	### Which mapping paths work
1141	
1142	- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
1143	- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
1144	- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
1145	- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
1146	- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.
1147	
1148	## Routing on tool results
1149	
1150	Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.
1151	
1152	```json
1153	{
1154	  "transitions": [
1155	    {
1156	      "target_node": "load_order",
1157	      "description": "The check passed",
1158	      "condition": {
1159	        "logic": "or",
1160	        "conditions": [
1161	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
1162	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
1163	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
1164	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
1165	        ]
1166	      }
1167	    }
1168	  ]
1169	}
1170	```
1171	
1172	Rules:
1173	
1174	- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
1175	- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
1176	- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.
1177	
1178	### Success and failure counters
1179	
1180	The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.
1181	
1182	| Placement | Variables |
1183	|---|---|
1184	| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
1185	| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |
1186	
1187	Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.
1188	
1189	```json
1190	{
1191	  "transitions": [
1192	    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
1193	    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
1194	  ]
1195	}
1196	```
1197	
1198	### `suppress_tool_results`
1199	
1200	A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.
1201	
1202	### Background tools
1203	
1204	A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.
1205	
1206	## Retries and timeouts
1207	
1208	| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
1209	|---|---|---|---|
1210	| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
1211	| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
1212	| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
1213	| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |
1214	
1215	`connect_retries` in detail:
1216	
1217	- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
1218	- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
1219	- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
1220	- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
1221	- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
1222	- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.
1223	
1224	The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.
1225	
1226	## Pre and post Python hooks
1227	
1228	An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.
1229	
1230	```json
1231	{
1232	  "type": "function",
1233	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
1234	  "function": {
1235	    "name": "check_answer",
1236	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
1237	    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
1238	    "parameters": {
1239	      "type": "object",
1240	      "properties": {
1241	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
1242	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
1243	        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
1244	      }
1245	    }
1246	  },
1247	  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
1248	  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
1249	}
1250	```
1251	
1252	| Hook | Names available | Use |
1253	|---|---|---|
1254	| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
1255	| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |
1256	
1257	Documented behaviour:
1258	
1259	- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
1260	- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
1261	- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
1262	- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.
1263	
1264	### What `result` looks like in a post-hook
1265	
1266	The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:
1267	
1268	- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
1269	- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
1270	- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
1271	- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.
1272	
1273	The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.
1274	
1275	Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.
1276	
1277	## Code nodes and `code_exec`
1278	
1279	A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.
1280	
1281	```json
1282	{
1283	  "name": "compute_delivery",
1284	  "node_type": "code",
1285	  "passthrough": true,
1286	  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
1287	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
1288	  "pre_actions": [
1289	    {
1290	      "type": "function",
1291	      "function": {
1292	        "name": "code_exec",
1293	        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
1294	        "parameters": {
1295	          "type": "object",
1296	          "properties": {
1297	            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
1298	            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
1299	          }
1300	        }
1301	      }
1302	    }
1303	  ],
1304	  "transitions": [
1305	    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
1306	  ]
1307	}
1308	```
1309	
1310	| Parameter | Meaning |
1311	|---|---|
1312	| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
1313	| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |
1314	
1315	### Reading and writing variables
1316	
1317	- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
1318	- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
1319	- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.
1320	
1321	Verified in a working builder:
1322	
1323	- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
1324	- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
1325	- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
1326	- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
1327	- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.
1328	
1329	### What a code node returns
1330	
1331	Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is
1332	
1333	```json
1334	{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
1335	```
1336	
1337	The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:
1338	
1339	| Variable | Value |
1340	|---|---|
1341	| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
1342	| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
1343	| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
1344	| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
1345	| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
1346	| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
1347	| `setup_success_count` | `1` |
1348	
1349	For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.
1350	
1351	### Rules for snippets
1352	
1353	- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
1354	- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
1355	- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
1356	- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
1357	- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
1358	- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.
1359	
1360	### Sandbox limits
1361	
1362	| Limit | Value |
1363	|---|---|
1364	| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
1365	| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
1366	| Network and file access | Not documented |
1367	| Memory and output size | Not documented |
1368	
1369	### `code_exec` as a tool
1370	
1371	`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.
1372	
1373	## Lifecycle tools
1374	
1375	A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.
1376	
1377	| Value | When |
1378	|---|---|
1379	| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
1380	| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
1381	| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |
1382	
1383	Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.
1384	
1385	```json
1386	{
1387	  "initial_node": "greeting",
1388	  "nodes": {},
1389	  "tools": [
1390	    {
1391	      "type": "function",
1392	      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
1393	      "function": {
1394	        "name": "push_call_result",
1395	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
1396	        "parameters": {
1397	          "type": "object",
1398	          "properties": {
1399	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
1400	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
1401	            "body": {
1402	              "type": "object",
1403	              "properties": {
1404	                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
1405	                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
1406	              }
1407	            }
1408	          }
1409	        }
1410	      }
1411	    }
1412	  ]
1413	}
1414	```
1415	
1416	Rules:
1417	
1418	- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
1419	- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
1420	- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
1421	- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
1422	- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
1423	- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).
1424	
1425	## Tool results and the next turn
1426	
1427	After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:
1428	
1429	- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
1430	- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.
1431	
1432	What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.
1433	
1434	Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.
1435	
1436	## Checklist
1437	
1438	- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
1439	- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
1440	- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
1441	- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
1442	- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
1443	- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
1444	- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
1445	- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
1446	- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.
1447	"""Freya schema constructors. Policy, paths, values and branch choices come from input sources.
1448	
1449	Import these from a builder-generated Python script, then json.dump the graph.
1450	These helpers do not infer business rules, attach services automatically, or alter exports.
1451	"""
1452	from copy import deepcopy
1453	
1454	
1455	def api_tool(name, url, method, body=None, mapping=None, description="", timeout_ms=30000):
1456	    """body is a JSON Schema object from the contract, with runtime/default bindings."""
1457	    if not url.startswith(("https://", "http://")) or method not in {"GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"}:
1458	        raise ValueError("Provide the actual source URL and HTTP method")
1459	    if body is not None and (not isinstance(body, dict) or body.get("type") != "object"):
1460	        raise ValueError("body must be an object schema, not a payload string")
1461	    properties = {
1462	        "url": {"type": "string", "default": url},
1463	        "method": {"type": "string", "default": method},
1464	        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
1465	    }
1466	    if body is not None:
1467	        properties["body"] = deepcopy(body)
1468	    tool = {"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": timeout_ms}, "function": {
1469	        "name": name, "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": description,
1470	        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": properties}}}
1471	    if mapping:
1472	        tool["response_mapping"] = deepcopy(mapping)
1473	    return tool
1474	
1475	
1476	def end_node(name, message=""):
1477	    """A real hang-up, independent of any bank record/close API."""
1478	    properties = {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "custom" if message else "none"}}
1479	    if message:
1480	        properties["spoken_message"] = {"type": "string", "default": message}
1481	    return {"name": name, "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
1482	            "disable_inactivity_monitor": True, "transitions": [], "terminal": {
1483	                "type": "function", "function": {"name": name, "handler": "__function__:end_call",
1484	                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": properties}}}}
1485	
1486	
1487	def action_node(name, tool, transitions, fallback):
1488	    """Run an action on entry; caller supplies response-dependent routes and fallback."""
1489	    action = deepcopy(tool)
1490	    mapping = action.pop("response_mapping", None)
1491	    if not fallback:
1492	        raise ValueError("Action nodes need a fallback branch derived from the source")
1493	    routes = deepcopy(transitions)
1494	    if not routes or routes[-1].get("condition", {}).get("operator") != "always":
1495	        routes.append({"target_node": fallback, "description": "Fallback after action result", "condition": {"operator": "always"}})
1496	    node = {"name": name, "node_type": "api_request", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
1497	            "passthrough": True, "passthrough_default_transition": fallback,
1498	            "pre_actions": [action], "transitions": routes}
1499	    if mapping:
1500	        node["response_mapping"] = mapping
